messages:
sam: FYI sampleapp CI red after auth/retry change merged. regendiff shows a bunch of ordering churn and a semver bump in the SDK package.json that I didn't expect.
ci-bot: [pipeline] https://ci.internal.redwood/teams/devex/pipelines/4523/builds/9876 — tests/regendiff failed :x:
maria: ugh. can you paste the regendiff snippet? might be the usual typegen sort nondeterminism but want to confirm.
sam: here's the top of the diff from the sampleapp repo (regendiff output):
```
-  "RetryPolicy": {
-    "maxAttempts": 3,
-    "backoff": "expo"
-  },
+  "RetryPolicy": {
+    "backoff": "expo",
+    "maxAttempts": 3
+  },
---
-  "openapi":{"components":{"schemas":{"AuthConfig":{"properties":{"authRetry": {"type":"boolean","default":true}}}}}}
+  "openapi":{"components":{"schemas":{"AuthConfig":{"properties":{"auth_retry": {"type":"boolean","default":true}}}}}}
```
sam: looks like two simultaneous things: property name normalization (camelCase -> snake_case) and property ordering flip. sampleapp ended up with a package.json patch bump because the SDK publish step saw a regen diff.
maria: that normalization change came from the auth/retry PR? I thought we only touched middleware ordering. @jacob any idea if codegen started normalizing names due to new JSON tags?
jacob: I dug in. The auth PR added a small helper that serializes server-side defaults through a JSON sanitizer we re-used from infra. That sanitizer applies snake_case -> so yes it accidentally changed the OpenAPI fixtures used for typegen. Separately, typegen's property iteration relies on map iteration so ordering isn't stable across runs. Combined, that produced the noisy regendiff + accidental semver bump.
jacob: short-term fix: revert the sanitizer usage in the fixtures for the generator and add a deterministic sort in typegen. Long-term: add an invariant test that regenerates on main and asserts no unintended diff for sampleapp.
maria: thanks. can you open a small PR with the revert + deterministic sort? also add a changelog note to explain we reverted an accidental normalization.
jacob: will do. PR will include: 
```bash
- scripts/regenerate.sh --target sampleapp
- // in typegen: Object.keys(props).sort() before emitting
```
liz: for the immediate CI unblocking — should we accept the current regendiff on the sampleapp pipeline and re-run publish after the PR? we don't want to ship a semver bump that isn't a real feature.
maria: yes — let's block the publish. @sam can you revert the package.json bump in sampleapp and hold the release until jacob's PR merges and we regenerate?
sam: on it. I'll revert the bump and land a temporary skip flag on the sampleapp publish job: 
```yaml
- name: publish-sampleapp
  if: contains(github.ref, 'main') && env.ALLOW_SAMPLEAPP_PUBLISH == 'true'
```
sam: then once jacob's PR lands I'll run: `./scripts/regenerate.sh && git add . && git commit -m "regen: fix ordering/names" && yarn publish --no-git-tag-version` and restart pipeline.
ci-bot: re-run request queued by sam — build 9877 scheduled :gear:
maria: extra ask: jacob, include a unit test in typegen that does 10 runs on a small fixture and asserts identical output. that will catch map-order flakes.
jacob: yes will add that. also adding a comment in the generator config documenting why we force alpha sort so future folks don't remove it thinking it's "redundant".
liz: once patched and regen'd I'll coordinate a quick smoke run on dedicated and hosted to ensure behavior is identical (auth behavior must not regress). I'll post the smoke link here.
sam: thanks all. open PR numbers? jacob and maria assign reviewers from devex and eng-runtime and tag me for the sampleapp revert.
jacob: PR 2437 (revert sanitizer + sort) coming in 30m. includes tests. :thumbsup:
maria: I'll review fast. thanks for quick turnaround everyone. :rocket:
liz: smoke run link after regen: https://smoke.internal.redwood/runs/5562 — all good so far :eyes:
sam: will re-run full CI once PR merges. closing this thread for now but will update if anything weird pops up.
